h: The Eyes of David and Bilam See Different Worlds

p: בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (רו, רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב)
In the holy Zohar on this parashah (beginning of 206b):
of the eye of David, etc.";
And the point is that David HaMelech, alav hashalom,
was a chariot for the middah of Malchus,
he looked with an evil eye,
were drawn from the eye of David;
הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה בִּכְלַל כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
that is, that he not be included in Knesses Yisrael;
for a metzora is sent out of the camp of Yisrael,
which is the holiness of Knesses Yisrael.
of whom it is written (Melachim II 5:27),
"And the tzara'as of Naaman shall cling to you
that he would never be healed
to return to the holiness of Knesses Yisrael
that he has no share in the World to Come,
since he is not included in "all Yisrael"
who have a share in the World to Come.
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי כָּל שֶׁנִּסְתַּכֵּל בּוֹ דָּוִד
And therefore all whom David looked at
such as the Pelishti and Yoav,
"Those who fear You will see me and rejoice";
for he was a chariot for the middah of Malchus,
like Shabbos, which is the middah of Malchus;
and "the Shabbos of Erev Shabbos is fear,
This is not so of Bilam:
for he was the opposite of Knesses Yisrael.
eleven things for which afflictions come,
also for an evil eye, etc.;
כָּל הָנֵי מִילִּין הֲווֹ וַדַּאי בְּבִלְעָם
all these things were certainly in Bilam.
חָשַׁב עַל ז׳ דְּבָרִים נְגָעִים בָּאִים
it lists seven things for which afflictions come;
seven are the days of the week";
That is, that for each middah
for which one is sent out of the camp of Yisrael;
but a metzora can be healed
But when one becomes sunk in sin,
the Mishnah (beginning of Perek Chelek) lists
who have no share in the World to Come,
from the holiness of Knesses Yisrael.
And against the middah of Malchus
they did not find an individual soul to list,
and they wished to count Shlomo,
who was a chariot for the middah of Malchus,
and in his days the moon was in its fullness;
and afterward it is written of him that he went astray;
and they thought he would be among them,
And a bas kol went forth,
"Shall it be according to your mind, etc.?" (Iyov 34:33),
and they counted Bilam against the middah of Malchus,
for he was the opposite of Knesses Yisrael,
the aspect of Malchus in holiness.
And the holy Zohar lists twelve things
according to the view of the eleven, as mentioned above;
corresponds to the twelve tribes of Kah;
alludes to the twelve tribes, as above;
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁבְּכָל שֵׁבֶט יֵשׁ חֵטְא כְּנֶגְדּוֹ
that is, for each tribe there is a corresponding sin
through which one becomes liable to be sent out
And it says that Bilam the wicked
בְּוַדַּאי הָיָה לוֹ כָּל הַי״ב חֲטָאִים
שֶׁהוּא הָיָה הַהֵיפֶךְ מִכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְגַמְרֵי
for he was the complete opposite of Knesses Yisrael.
And the expounders of allusions said
that all of them come to the World to Come
that is, only the three kings
that there is some hint and mark in the Torah,
And the point is that although it appears
that they were sent out of the community of Knesses Yisrael,
and those lost in the land of Ashur shall come" (Yeshayahu 27:13)
even though they were completely assimilated among the nations,
וּבְוַדַּאי עָבְרוּ עַל כָּל הַשִּׁשָּׁה חֲטָאִים
and certainly transgressed all six sins
reckoned as causing loss through them
of a share in the World to Come;
and likewise "those cast away in the land of Mitzrayim,"
who were surrounded by the kelipah
like a fetus in its mother's womb
will awaken their hearts to teshuvah,
and they will come to the World to Come.
This is not so of Bilam,
from the community of Knesses Yisrael;
and therefore the expounders of allusions
as appears from the Gemara there.
that regarding what the Arizal asked,
"May my soul die the death of the upright,"
and he was killed by the sword
as having no share in the World to Come;
and it was to them that he referred
in all the praises with which he praised them;
for with the upright of Yisrael
he did not merit at all to grasp their stature.
And he asked, "May my soul die the death of the upright,"
בֵּין אֵלּוּ שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
among those who have no share in the World to Come,
בֵּין פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל כָּל פָּנִים
among the sinners of Yisrael at least.
And so we find regarding Shimshon,
"Let my soul die with the Pelishtim"
as referring to the death of the soul,
that he has no share in the World to Come,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קכז, א)
through the Men of the Great Assembly,
who counted three kings and four commoners;
for they knew there had to be seven sins
through which one can go so astray
that he is not included in
וּכְנֶגֶד כָּל אֶחָד יֵשׁ נֶפֶשׁ אַחַת
and corresponding to each there is one soul;
and they did not find in Yisrael
one against the middah of Knesses Yisrael,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין לוֹ פֵּירוּשׁ כְּלָל לִכְאוֹרָה
which seemingly makes no sense at all,
since they opened with "All Yisrael, etc.,"
and one of them is Bilam
what is Bilam's business within Klal Yisrael,
that it should tell us that he has no share
But this was to fulfill his request,
"May my soul die the death of the upright."
for the expounders of allusions found a hint
that they will have a share
(and this was explained in the previous maamar as well).
And this is what the Baal HaTurim says:
that of Balak it is written "went on his way,"
and of Bilam it is written "returned to his place" (Bamidbar 24:25):
that he was driven from his way
for then he returned to his place,
which is the place of impurity,
and, as it were, Hashem Yisbarach
and from then he was driven out
from the World to Come forever.
